name: Black Olive
lede: Black Olive is a very dark, slightly green-grey neutral, the color of a ripe olive that has almost lost its green.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name is a plain description, and the swatch sits at ISCC-NBS block 108, a very dark olive-grey, with the RAL paint code 6015 as a close commercial match [1]. It is near [[olive]] in hue but far darker, and close to [[black]] in lightness [1].

The books we hold mention black olives only as food. Livingstone describes a patient who lost all color vision after a brain injury and ate only achromatic foods, black olives among them, because they looked normal to him [3]. That says something about how dark and unsaturated the fruit is, but nothing about the color name's history [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Black Olive appears in 8.21% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed [2]. It is more common than 93% of the named colors, and it peaks in the 1900s at 8.1% of that century's paintings [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone, in 48% of cases [2]. The painter who leans on it most is Arnoud van Halen, in 16 of 50 works here [2]. Dark varnish and aged canvases push many browns toward this swatch, so these numbers describe photographs [2].
